subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should OpenClaw mobile apps support arbitrary per-gateway proxy headers, or should the mobile proxy-auth surface be narrowed to typed schemes such as Basic, Bearer, or fixed Cloudflare-style service-token fields first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary controls credentials sent before Gateway auth, mobile secure storage, diagnostics redaction, reset/forget behavior, TLS expectations, and whether arbitrary operator-supplied headers are safe in native app settings.

options.title: Approve broad custom headers with security review
options.body: Land the platform PRs only after owner/security reviewers approve the sanitizer, secure-store lifecycle, gateway-only attachment, redaction, reset, TLS, and real-proxy proof contract.

options.title: Narrow to typed proxy auth
options.body: Ask the platform PRs to replace arbitrary name/value headers with a smaller typed credential model that is easier to validate, redact, clear, and document.

options.title: Defer native proxy credentials
options.body: Keep the mobile apps unsupported for authenticating-proxy deployments while maintainers settle the cross-platform transport-auth design.

recommendation.title: Approve broad custom headers with security review
recommendation.body: Land the platform PRs only after owner/security reviewers approve the sanitizer, secure-store lifecycle, gateway-only attachment, redaction, reset, TLS, and real-proxy proof contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored and is assigned to the canonical issue, opened the current iOS and Android implementation PRs, and has the strongest recent product/security signal for this mobile Gateway boundary.
